rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Connection between Total Internal Reflection and other topics  ·  Key Formula 5: Important relation in Total Internal Reflection  ·  ❌ The critical angle exists for any pair of media. ✅ The critical angle only exists when $n_1 > n_2$. If light goes from air to glass ($n_1 < n_2$), there is no critical angle — refraction always occurs.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ At the critical angle, all light is reflected. ✅ At the critical angle ($i = \theta_c$), the refracted ray travels ALONG the boundary ($r = 90°$). TIR begins only when $i > \theta_c$, not at $i = \theta_c$.  ·  ❌ TIR produces a dimmer reflection than a mirror. ✅ TIR reflects 100% of the light — it is BRIGHTER than any metallic mirror, which typically absorbs 5–15% of incident light.  ·  ❌ Optical fibres work because light is "trapped" by the cladding. ✅ Optical fibres work because of TIR at the core-cladding interface. The cladding has a LOWER refractive index than the core, creating the condition for TIR.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The critical angle for diamond is about 42°. ✅ Diamond's critical angle is about 24.4° (much smaller than glass's 42°). This small critical angle is what makes diamonds so brilliant — light undergoes multiple TIR events before exiting.  ·  ❌ TIR can occur at any interface, including solid-solid interfaces. ✅ TIR requires a boundary between two media with DIFFERENT refractive indices. It can occur at any such boundary (glass-air, water-glass, fibre core-cladding) as long as light travels from the higher-index to the lower-index medium.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Total Internal Reflection
